title: Terminal-proof discipline embedded in per-turn directive capsule
bullets: Every session now starts with a proof-over-appearance directive in the per-turn capsule, so agents verify claims with evidence before reporting work done.

The terminal-proof protocol now lives as permanent operating discipline woven through AGENTS.md's verification standards, blast-radius management, and a new final-state verification gate instead of a standalone block.
The same directive ships through the OpenCode fallback and the pi runtime hook chain, so the reminder stays consistent across executors.

title: Six-Runtime Surface Audit Complete
bullets: The repository's runtime support story is now audited end-to-end, with 20+ stale sites still naming only Claude/Codex/OpenCode mapped against the six surfaces that actually ship.
Real gaps are separated from non-issues: sk-code's surface detection and the terminal-proof packet are confirmed clean, so follow-up work targets only genuine stale sites.
The support set is fixed: copilot is removed as deprecated rather than labeled legacy, and generated agent mirrors are regenerated instead of hand-edited to avoid drift.
A scoped plan with acceptance criteria is approved and implementation is queued for the next work session.

title: Communication-quality rules in one place
bullets: Every runtime now follows one consistent set of communication-quality rules, anchored in a dedicated AGENTS.md §8 section covering writing, recommendations, and turn framing.
The Codex voice spec was reconciled with the root rules, so the two files no longer drift apart.
Only genuinely missing craft principles were added, so existing guidance remained consistent and un-contradicted.

title: AGENTS.md Audit: Leaner Guidance, Corrected Routing
bullets: AGENTS.md is now leaner and safer to follow: a five-iteration bloat audit surfaced 40 findings (~13.5% removable lines), and the verified-safe subset cut redundant lines and fixed all seven broken constitutional links.
Runtime agent routing is now complete and correct: the agent-directory resolution table gained the previously missing Cursor and Devin rows, matching the rest of the framework.
Obsolete dispatch rules for Fable subagents and Open Design were removed from AGENTS.md and BARTER.md, so agents no longer act on outdated routing.
Advisor metadata placement guidance now matches the authoritative skill-root contract, avoiding misconfigured hub-versus-standalone skill roots.

title: cli-external hub unifies both dispatch workflows
bullets: Invoke both CLI-dispatch workflows — cli-opencode and cli-claude-code — from one new cli-external parent hub instead of two unrelated top-level skills.
Dispatch behavior is unchanged: both workflows relocate and re-register as hub modes without any change to dispatch semantics.
Executor delegation keeps resolving correctly because the routing scorer now sources its alias table from the hub's mode registry instead of a top-level family filter.

title: Codex CLI revived with full lifecycle parity
bullets: Use Codex CLI as a third dispatch executor in deep-loop workflows, with routes failing closed whenever the codex binary is unavailable.

Codex sessions now receive the same lifecycle guardrails as Claude and OpenCode, including spec-gate enforcement, code-graph freshness, post-edit quality, dispatch audit, completion evidence, and session cleanup.
The Codex agent set is auto-generated from your canonical OpenCode agents and parity-checked on demand, so the two never drift apart.
Codex fast-tier dispatches support four models (gpt-5.5 default plus gpt-5.6-luna/terra/sol) with per-model reasoning ceilings, all 20 model-by-effort combinations verified live.
Codex hook installation is now self-healing: a convergent installer reconciles the global hooks file idempotently, refuses linked-worktree anchors, and a cross-runtime watchdog flags drift.

title: CLI hub canonicalized under cli-external-orchestration
bullets: The external CLI hub now lives at the canonical cli-external-orchestration directory, with full git history preserved through the rename.
Skill-advisor routing now recognizes the canonical hub path while continuing to resolve cli-opencode as its concrete executor.
All live references were repointed to the canonical hub, keeping executor-level names like cli-opencode intact where they are semantically correct.

title: Revive Devin CLI as a first-class executor
bullets: Dispatch coding sessions to Cognition's Devin CLI as a new executor mode, including multi-model coding, subagent delegation, cloud handoff, and cross-AI validation.

Run the same spec-kit hook guards inside Devin sessions, with dispatch preflight, edit quality, code-graph freshness, MCP route, task dispatch, and permission guards now firing across all supported runtimes.
Review code with any of the repo's 13 agents mirrored into native Devin subagent profiles, invoked through the cli-devin skill.
Verify Devin integration with the shipped 20-scenario manual-testing playbook covering invocation, subagents, hooks, permission modes, rules, and MCP.

title: Cursor CLI is now a first-class dispatch executor
bullets: Route work to Cursor's CLI as a new first-class executor: cli-cursor is the fourth cli-external-orchestration mode, so you can say “delegate to cursor” and hand a task to cursor-agent.
Use cursor-agent as a deep-loop executor kind with fail-closed preflight checks, so an unavailable binary never becomes routable and approval/sandbox flags map correctly.
Get prompt-craft guidance for Composer-2.5, Cursor's native model, which now ships as a registered profile in sk-prompt/prompt-models.
Run Spec Kit gates inside Cursor sessions: new Cursor hook adapters enforce the spec gate on Cursor tool calls, with the deny contract verified live.
Mirror your repo agents into Cursor, which auto-imports Claude-format subagents, and rely on a 19-scenario manual-testing playbook covering Cursor's live CLI surface.

title: Pi CLI joins as cli-pi executor
bullets: You can now drive Pi CLI (pi.dev) as a first-class executor: cli-pi is the sixth mode in the cli-external-orchestration hub, shipped with a full skill packet (SKILL.md, references, assets, and prompt templates) to guide the workflow.
Deep-loop and model-benchmark tooling now recognize cli-pi as a sixth executor kind and fail closed instead of guessing when the pi binary or its invocation contract can't be verified.
You can connect real MCP servers to Pi over stdio via a committed .pi/mcp.json — live-confirmed working, entirely offline and independent of any provider API key.
Pi dispatches are locked to a fail-closed allowlist of 7 operator-confirmed models, with prompt-craft guidance added for deepseek-v4-pro, MiniMax-M3, and mimo-v2.5-pro.

title: Per-mode provider and model reference catalogs
bullets: Each of the six CLI modes now has a single reference file that answers which providers, models, effort tiers, and invocation commands to use, instead of that knowledge being scattered across multiple docs.
Smart routing now covers all six CLI modes instead of only three, so the right per-mode guidance surfaces no matter which executor you dispatch.

Mode reference and skill docs were trimmed of duplicated model tables, leaving a compact default-plus-effort summary that points to the new catalog while keeping safety-critical details like cursor's allowlist readable inline.
The hub's own skill and README docs now point directly at the per-mode catalogs for provider and model guidance.

title: cli-pi fanout now accepts deepseek-v4-flash
bullets: You can now route a fanout `cli-pi` dispatch to `deepseek-v4-flash` for latency-optimized turns, where the enforced allowlist previously rejected it.
cli-opencode already exposed the model and needed no change; cli-cursor and cli-devin remain unchanged because their providers offer no DeepSeek V4 Flash id at all.
The model id was live-confirmed on the pi install before being added, honoring the roster's read-from-live, never-fabricated contract.

title: Qwen 3.8 Max now dispatchable via opencode-go
bullets: You can now run Qwen 3.8 Max through cli-pi fan-out dispatch, since the model is whitelisted in the enforced roster.
DeepSeek V4 Flash now routes through the opencode-go gateway by default, using the subsidized 2x-usage endpoint for cheaper dispatches.
The direct --provider deepseek route for Flash still works, so nothing about existing dispatch behavior is removed.
The cli-pi and cli-opencode provider docs now show the opencode-go dispatch shape for both models, each backed by a live verified run.

title: Portable plain-English CLI communication projection
bullets: Enable the new sk-communication skill to get terse agent output rewritten into plain English while the canonical output stays byte-for-byte unchanged.
Projection is off by default with a private per-machine opt-in, so nothing changes until you explicitly enable it.
A compatibility doctor diagnoses versions, capabilities, and privacy facts before you flip the switch.
Provider and runtime adapters extend projection across CLIs, and content-free processing keeps raw content and credentials out of the pipeline.

title: Pi Remote Mobile Agent planning foundation
bullets: A private, Claude-app-style mobile control plane over Pi CLI is now planned end-to-end across an approved nine-phase program, giving the team an execution roadmap before any code ships.

Each of the nine phases owns an independently executable planning packet with bounded scope, measurable requirements, evidence gates, rollback, and phase handoffs, so every workstream can be run and verified on its own.
The contract and threat baseline is pinned up front, so security-sensitive surfaces such as auth, the tailnet boundary, and remote mutation are specified before implementation begins.

The program covers the full pipeline to release, from an automated test harness and relay protocol with durable state to the mobile PWA, approval and containment, push hardening, operator runbooks, and release verification.

title: Pi remote experience parity research complete
bullets: Completed a two-lineage deep-research run that converged on the target shape for the Pi remote experience: a typed, redacted, replayable event ledger with a separate authenticated command protocol, not a terminal mirror or chat clone.
Ranked P0/P1/P2 recommendations are ready to amend the 041 packet, including typed relay envelopes, exact-action approval events, content-free attention, and first-class pending states.

title: Gemini CLI orchestration skill for cross-AI tasks
bullets: Claude Code and OpenCode can now delegate cross-AI work to Google's Gemini CLI through a dedicated cli-gemini skill.
A smart router scores your request across 7 intents to load only the relevant references, keeping context lean and avoiding wasted tokens.
The skill ships with 9 Gemini agent delegation options, 10 integration patterns, and copy-paste prompt templates ready for reuse.
Routing to the Gemini CLI is reliable, with skill-advisor boosters resolving 'use gemini' queries at 0.95 confidence.

title: New cli-codex skill and cli-gemini consolidation
bullets: Codex CLI now joins the other CLI bridges via the new `cli-codex` skill, so you can drive it through the same documentation-driven pattern you already use.
`cli-gemini` guidance now points to a single canonical Gemini model, removing avoidable model-selection ambiguity.
The new skill is discoverable through the updated advisor and README registration surfaces, keeping the CLI bridge family consistent.

title: New cli-claude-code skill for external AI delegation
bullets: External AI assistants (Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Copilot) can now delegate coding and reasoning tasks to Claude Code CLI through a new cli-claude-code skill.
Smart intent routing maps 7 signals to the right references, defaulting to DEEP_REASONING so calls land on Claude Code's extended-thinking strength.
Ready-made reference materials cover all CLI flags, 3 model tiers (opus/sonnet/haiku), 9 agent delegation patterns, and a comparison table against Gemini and Codex.
Ten prompt-template categories (code review, bug fixing, test generation, and more) are copy-paste ready via the claude -p pattern.
Orchestration is reversed from the sibling cli-gemini and cli-codex skills: your external AI stays the conductor while Claude Code executes.

title: New cli-copilot skill for Copilot delegation
bullets: Any AI assistant can now delegate coding tasks to GitHub's Copilot CLI through a new structured skill with smart routing and reference materials.
The skill unlocks Copilot's unique multi-provider model access (7+ models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google) with documented selection guidance.
It supports plan mode, autonomous autopilot execution, and delegation of work to GitHub's cloud infrastructure.
It ships with 10 prompt-template categories, orchestration patterns, and a 4-way CLI comparison that completes the cross-AI ecosystem alongside cli-gemini, cli-codex, and cli-claude-code.

title: CLI bridges guard against self-invocation
bullets: CLI bridge skills now warn when a runtime tries to delegate to the bridge that targets itself, preventing circular delegation loops.
Each runtime is pointed back to its own native capabilities instead of receiving a generic warning, making the guard actionable.
Consistent anti-self-delegation guidance now applies across cli-claude-code, cli-gemini, cli-codex, and cli-copilot.

title: Prompt-quality cards and /prompt agent mode
bullets: Every CLI skill now runs a pre-dispatch prompt-quality check against a local prompt-quality card, so prompts reach the CLI executor at a consistent quality bar instead of ad-hoc wording.

High-complexity and compliance-sensitive prompts now escalate to a dedicated @improve-prompt agent that improves them in fresh context, avoiding caller-context pollution from loading the full prompt-engineering skill inline.
The /prompt command now supports Inline mode for ordinary interactive use and Agent mode for fresh-context improvement when complexity_hint >= 7 or isolation is requested.
All four CLI prompt-template assets now carry Framework: annotations and load the quality card on every dispatch, keeping template metadata and the quality card in sync.

title: Codex voice personalization
bullets: Every Codex CLI session now loads a personal voice addendum (Voice, Tone, Reasoning Visibility) from a shared, version-controlled file.
Codex responses become more natural: no filler openers, hedged phrasing when unsure, reasoning before conclusions, and named trade-offs.
The addendum combines with your project's AGENTS.md framework, so gates, scope lock, safety, and memory rules still apply unchanged.
The file is version-controlled at the repo root and symlinked into your home directory, so edits propagate to all future sessions automatically.
AI orchestrators delegating to Codex keep their own voice governance and are not injected with this content, avoiding redundant, token-wasteful prompts.

title: cli-opencode skill for external OpenCode dispatch
bullets: Delegate coding, review, or research to a detached OpenCode CLI session from any other runtime (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) and receive structured handback, via the new cli-opencode skill.
The skill self-guards against recursion: it detects when it already runs inside an OpenCode-managed session (env vars, process ancestry, lock-file probe) and refuses to spawn a nested one.
cli-opencode joins the four existing CLI executor skills as a discoverable peer, ranked at confidence 0.95 by the skill advisor without special token boosting.

title: Manual testing playbooks for five CLI orchestrators
bullets: Validate cli-gemini, cli-claude-code, cli-codex, cli-copilot, and cli-opencode end-to-end against 129 per-feature scenarios spread across 40 numbered category folders, so you no longer invent test cases by hand.
Compare any two sibling CLIs directly, because the shared category numbering (invocation, integration patterns, prompt templates) reads identically in every playbook.

Grade each CLI surface deterministically with 9-column pass/fail scenario tables, CLEAR-card prompt-template grading, and per-agent/model/tool coverage spanning session continuity, sandbox modes, cost caps, and cloud delegation.

title: Provider realignment and auth pre-flight
bullets: CLI dispatches now default to `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro --variant high`, the highest-capability reasoning model on the opencode-go gateway at low cost.
The `github-copilot` provider is no longer documented as a dispatch option in the cli-opencode skill.
Direct DeepSeek API models (`deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`) remain fully supported and unchanged.
A one-shot Provider Auth Pre-Flight now detects missing credentials before dispatching and asks you which model to use instead of silently swapping providers.

title: cli-* skills: consistent auth checks and invocation
bullets: All five cli-* skills (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini, OpenCode) now share the same §3 structure, so you get a consistent Default Invocation block showing the pinned model and flags for each CLI.

Each skill gained a Provider Auth Pre-Flight that detects whether you're authenticated before dispatch and uses an ASK-not-substitute decision tree instead of failing mid-run, invalidating cache when an auth error occurs mid-dispatch.
Cli-Copilot also gained an Error Handling table alongside the shared sections.

Every provider-native detail is preserved, including each CLI's own detection command, auth method, and flags (e.g. --effort, --yolo, native agent-routing syntax), so no unique per-skill value prop was collapsed.

title: Remove mcp-clickup skill, keep ClickUp via Code Mode
bullets: mcp-clickup is no longer a bundled skill, trimming the skill set from 22 to 21.
ClickUp work is unaffected: calls flow through Code Mode's clickup manual and the upstream mcp-clickup package, so task creation and other service features keep working.
Advisor routing and README listings now stay consistent, so nothing recommends or points at the removed skill.

title: Cli-codex preferred for routing-trace consumption
bullets: Agents now prefer cli-codex (gpt-5.5) for tasks that consume routing-trace resource paths literally, cutting wrong-path risk from cli-copilot's 11.1% to cli-codex's 66.7% accuracy.
cli-copilot's guidance now warns agents to treat its routing trace as advisory only, so it stays a reliable general-purpose dispatcher.
sk-doc/SKILL.md now publishes the per-CLI routing accuracy comparison (cli-codex 66.7% / cli-opencode 47.2% / cli-copilot 11.1%), so the recommended default is backed by measured evidence.

title: cli-copilot removed after Copilot price hike
bullets: The Copilot CLI executor skill is gone — GitHub's price hike made cli-codex (gpt-5.5) the cheaper path, so you can no longer dispatch `cli-copilot`.
Ask the skill advisor for "copilot" and you'll now get cli-claude-code, the nearest remaining peer, instead of a dead skill.
The multi-ai-council agent no longer lists Copilot as a vantage across the .opencode, .claude, .gemini, and .codex runtimes.

title: Non-interactive cli-opencode dispatch no longer hangs
bullets: Deep-research and deep-review automation now completes in minutes instead of hanging for 12+ minutes at 0% CPU with zero output.
All four deep-research/deep-review YAML workflows now redirect stdin (`</dev/null`), fixing the hang when `opencode run` is dispatched non-interactively.
The cli-opencode skill now documents that every non-interactive dispatch requires `</dev/null`, including patterns for pipes, file redirects, and read loops.
The full deep-research loop that previously wasted ~3 hours across 14 hung attempts now finishes all 10 iterations in about 50 minutes.

title: New cli-devin skill for peer Devin dispatch
bullets: Dispatch tasks to Cognition's Devin for Terminal as a peer executor from any supported assistant (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, or a raw shell).
Get a copy-pasteable devin invocation that defaults to the SWE-1.6 coding model in the safe "normal" permission mode.
Hand off long-running local work to Devin's cloud with a 5-check operator-confirmation gate that must pass before any cloud-handoff dispatch.
Use the permission-mode risk taxonomy to map Devin modes to Codex sandbox levels and Claude/OpenCode --dangerously-skip-permissions.
Route "delegate to devin" requests to the new skill from any sibling cli-* skill now that the skill-advisor graph links them bidirectionally.

title: More reliable Devin deep-loop iterations
bullets: Deep research and review iterations now force step-by-step reasoning via sequential_thinking, making each iteration's output more deliberate and reliable.
Iteration agents are now limited to writing only the two files they actually need, reducing the blast radius of accidental edits.
The deep-loop dispatchers now detect and surface tool-rejection errors from the Devin runtime instead of letting them fail silently.
These cli-devin v1.0.4.0 improvements apply to future deep-loop runs and leave any in-flight iterations untouched.

title: cli-devin: data-driven RCAF prompt defaults
bullets: cli-devin SWE-1.6 dispatches now default to the RCAF (Role/Context/Action/Format) prompt scaffold, which scored 33% higher than the previous STAR baseline across 42 real dispatches.

Medium-density pre-planning (3-4 steps) is now the shared guidance across the sk-prompt master card and the four sibling CLI prompt-quality cards, replacing dense pre-planning that measurably underperformed.
The winning guidance was validated across models — RCAF wins, bundle-gate-aversion wording, and framework-driven anti-hallucination all hold on SWE-1.6, deepseek-v4-pro, and kimi-k2.6.

title: MiniMax 2.7 optimized providers and prompts
bullets: Dispatch MiniMax through cli-opencode and you now get the subscription Token Plan provider by default (MiniMax-M3-highspeed, falling back to MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed), which works on current installs where the old pay-per-token default errored.
The pay-per-token MiniMax Direct API stays available as the explicit `minimax` provider, so both billing modes coexist.
MiniMax 2.7 is now a first-class small-model option in cli-opencode and the shared sk-prompt-models registry, selectable directly.
MiniMax dispatches now use the TIDD-EC prompt framework with dense pre-planning, chosen by benchmarking five frameworks on the real MiniMax M2.7 model.

title: MiMo-V2.5-Pro now a selectable executor
bullets: Select Xiaomi MiMo-V2.5-Pro through the new xiaomi-token-plan-ams provider in cli-opencode, mirroring the existing MiniMax Token Plan wiring.
Run deep research, review, and improvement loops on MiMo or MiniMax token-plan models now that the hard-coded --agent general flag they rejected is gone from the dispatch paths.
Use the COSTAR prompt framework for MiMo dispatch — benchmarked as the best of five frameworks on real MiMo-V2.5-Pro (RACE a statistical tie).
Keep the current default (deepseek-v4-pro) unchanged, since MiMo is an additive, explicitly-selectable option rather than a replacement.
MiMo is the opposite of MiniMax on guardrail-heavy prompting, so its dispatch follows COSTAR-style lean-to-medium pre-planning instead of MiniMax's guardrail-heavy style.

title: Gemini executor, runtime, and model removed
bullets: The deprecated `cli-gemini` executor, its skill, and the checked-in project `.gemini` runtime are gone, so every command now dispatches only to supported executors.
Gemini is no longer a recognized host runtime, so hooks and runtime detection advertise only supported runtimes instead of claiming a Gemini path exists.
`gemini-flash` is removed as a fallback model, so no deep-loop or model-benchmark surface routes work through it.
Commands, docs, feature catalogs, and changelogs no longer present Gemini as an available option for new work.
Your external Gemini-CLI state in the home directory is untouched; only the framework's checked-in Gemini surface was removed.

title: cli-devin skill removed from dispatch
bullets: The cli-devin skill is fully removed, so Devin is no longer available as a CLI dispatch executor.
Route work that previously used Devin through the remaining cli-opencode executor instead.
Devin-specific runtime hooks, executor enums, and skill-advisor entries are gone, so no dispatch or routing path can target the deprecated executor.
Docs, agents, and governance references were swept clean so nothing still points at the removed skill.

title: Kimi K2.7 Code first-class small model
bullets: You can now dispatch Kimi K2.7 Code (kimi-for-coding/k2p7) as a first-class small model through cli-opencode and sk-prompt-models, with the older kimi-k2.6 entry retired in its place.

Kimi K2.7 dispatches now default to the COSTAR prompt framework with TIDD-EC as the fallback, after a strict-validator bakeoff showed the model is framework-robust and retired the weaker rcaf framing.

If Kimi K2.7 appears to hang on broad or large-repo tasks, it may be over-exploring and hitting a 600s timeout that yields no output; add a hard read-cap to the prompt and allow a 1200s+ timeout, or drop --variant high.

title: GLM-5.2: new multimodal small model with COSTAR guidance
bullets: Dispatch GLM-5.2 as a first-class small model via the `zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2` slug or the `glm`/`zai` aliases, billed against your independent Z.AI GLM Coding Plan quota.
Prompt-framework questions for GLM-5.2 now route to empirically verified COSTAR guidance (TIDD-EC as fallback, avoid RCAF), backed by a 45-dispatch benchmark with no LLM-judge bias.

Use GLM-5.2's native vision for vision-to-code by sending images as base64 to the Z.AI Coding Plan API, since `opencode --file` image attachment stays broken for this provider (issue #20802) and the direct-API workaround is documented.
Budget generous timeouts for GLM-5.2 requests — observed latency spans 6-161s with thinking on — and retry the rare transient dispatch failure (~1/45).

title: cli-codex retired from active dispatch
bullets: Stop using cli-codex for external Codex dispatch — the executor is retired, and the skill advisor now routes such requests to supported skills instead.
If you use Codex Desktop, you can still read repo context through the new project bridge (.codex/config.toml plus specs, changelog, and skills symlinks) without the retired executor.
Codex hook support and generic Codex runtime references are removed from active commands, hooks, and skills; only OpenCode plugins and Claude Code hooks remain supported.

title: Hook reference docs relocated to owning trees
bullets: Four hook reference docs (goal-plugin, injection-contract, skill-advisor-hook, and its validation doc) now live in the trees that own them instead of one flat system-spec-kit folder.
All 34 live consumers were repointed to the new owner paths, so no working references to the old locations remain.
Renames preserved git history via git mv, and the relocation passes strict validation with zero warnings.
A follow-up sweep confirmed no ghost references to the old paths survive in live trees.

title: Per-prompt injection bloat reduction groundwork shipped
bullets: Per-prompt injection bloat is now measured and reducible across all six runtime hook adapters through verified, flag-gated candidates that keep the legacy full-directive output byte-identical until activated.

OpenCode prompts can show a fixed three-target compiled-route summary with a "+K more" count and SHA-256 digest instead of the full target list, fully recoverable on demand via revealCompiledRouteSummaryTargets.

Repeated deliveries of the same directive block, Gate-3 relay, and Pi subagent dispatch directive are now suppressed in shadow, keyed by session/epoch/content-hash receipts that fall open to full delivery on any ambiguity.
A delivery-receipt and byte-parity measurement foundation proves the reductions emit identical output across 30 serializer/case combinations before any default-on rollout.
A fail-open activation matrix, risk register, rollback procedures, and behavioral negative controls gate any future activation of the candidates.

title: Session goals across Devin, Cursor, and Pi
bullets: Your active session goal now carries into Devin, Cursor, and Pi CLI sessions: the goal brief is injected into prompts and restored at session start in every runtime.
Devin hooks check goal progress at stop points and can block continuation when the goal is unmet, while Pi records turn-end verification verdicts (observe-only).
Dispatch auditing now recognizes codex, devin, cursor-agent, and pi print-mode command lines, so dispatch checks fire on those runtimes too.
The unified hooks tree now mirrors the real OpenCode plugins as browsability symlinks, making the full plugin set visible inside each hook tree.

title: Goal-hook playbooks and live validation for every CLI
bullets: You now get manual-testing playbooks for the goal hook in all five goal-capable CLI runtimes (Devin, Cursor, Pi, OpenCode, Claude Code) plus the shared manage CLI, so you can verify goal-state injection in your runtime.
Live, canary-proven checks confirm the active-goal injection reaches the model turn on Pi and Devin, where the canary token was quoted verbatim in the model's own output.
For Cursor, the hook fires but the injection is invisible to the model by design, and this is now documented as the expected RECORDED-EVIDENCE result rather than a failure.
OpenCode's native mk-goal and Claude-native /goal cannot be validated headlessly, and those structural limits are now documented instead of claimed as working.

title: PI input hook: in-process advisor, instant repeats
bullets: PI message sends no longer block on a synchronous process-spawn chain, since the advisor lifecycle now runs in-process.
Repeat prompts now resolve in about 1 ms from the advisor's cache, down from 1.37–1.49 s per message.
A cache-invalidation bug was fixed so cached recommendations actually hit while genuinely removed skills still refresh.
The skill-advisor build no longer emits PI hook files with type errors.
PI hook wiring docs now describe the in-process path instead of the old spawn-based flow.

title: Spec-folder question only asks when needed
bullets: Read-only turns no longer re-surface the SPEC FOLDER QUESTION, so you only get asked when a turn actually looks like an answer, while write-time gate enforcement stays fully intact.
When the question does re-appear on a failed answer attempt, the A–D options now tell you to reply with the folder path, matching the grammar your answer is parsed against.

Adapters strip embedded session history and injected directive capsules before classification, so the gate stays closed on genuinely read-only turns instead of falsely opening on trigger-word lookalikes.
Answer grammar tightened: a bare "D" no longer silently skips the gate (pathless D re-asks for the folder) and the skip letter is now "E", matching the menu.

title: Pi-only subagent dispatch directive with governor parity
bullets: Pi now routes subagent work through native pi-subagents by default, using cli-* executors only when you explicitly request that mode.

Dispatch-shaped calls to cli-* executors are denied by default unless you explicitly authorize them or a deep-loop executor is in play, so unauthorized external CLI dispatch is fail-closed while native subagent tools keep working.
The skill-advisor bridge now emits the governor capsule identically to the canonical renderer across runtimes, so the governor directive stays consistent between OpenCode and Pi.
Dispatch preflight now parses quoted executor names correctly, so commands that quote the executor dispatch to the right executor instead of being misread.

title: Reasonix-style Pi prompt caching split
bullets: Pi's prompt caching is now split cleanly by provider: deep-pi owns DeepSeek's direct API while pi-cache-optimizer handles everything else, verified with zero overlap and no regression in live sessions.

deep-pi now tracks real economics — persistent per-session and daily stats plus a machine-readable report on every /deeppi call — and clearly separates measured costs from an explicitly labeled no-cache counterfactual savings estimate.

deep-pi's previously silent diagnostics now surface and reset per session, it warns once instead of staying dark when it sees an unrecognized DeepSeek model id, and invalid usage or failed turns no longer corrupt telemetry.
Both extensions are now vendored in-repo with a report-only provenance check, so Pi needs no external repository or npm dependency to run them.

title: Goal state isolated per workspace, runtime, session
bullets: Run one goal per workspace/runtime/session scope, so concurrent goals no longer overwrite each other across sessions or runtimes.
Pi registers the native /goal-pi command through its own session manager, and Cursor receives goal context scoped by session identity.
Goal archives are locked to the real state root, so stored goal ids cannot escape or corrupt other files.
Legacy singleton goal state no longer auto-loads: existing goals must be explicitly migrated or archived.

title: Unified kill-switch for all hooks
bullets: Disable every hook at once by setting MK_HOOKS_DISABLED, or switch off an individual concern with its own MK_<CONCERN>_DISABLED flag.
Existing kill-switch variables (goal, dispatch, skill-advisor, completion, spec-memory, spec-gate) still work as aliases, so current operator config keeps functioning unchanged.
The mcp-route-guard hook now respects these kill-switches on all six runtimes, so a disabled guard is truly silent everywhere.
Flag behavior is identical whether hooks load as CJS, ESM, or TypeScript, so no module-system surprises.

title: mcp-tooling hub unifies Chrome DevTools, ClickUp, Figma
bullets: Chrome DevTools, ClickUp, and Figma MCP bridges now resolve under one mcp-tooling hub that the skill advisor routes to, giving you a single canonical entry point for all three.

You can now browse the full Chrome DevTools capability surface from a new feature catalog and a byte-true snapshot of its Code Mode manuals, with Figma and ClickUp keeping their read-only transport posture and versions intact.
ClickUp gains a top-level install guide and Figma gains worked example walkthroughs, closing the discoverability gaps between the three bridge skills.

title: Aside browser automation bridge joins mcp-tooling
bullets: Drive the Aside AI automation browser from the mcp-tooling hub as a fourth mode, using the agentic `aside` CLI with an Aside-MCP-through-Code-Mode fallback.
Get intent-aware routing for TASK, REPL, MCP, INSTALL, and TROUBLESHOOT prompts, so Aside-browser phrasing resolves to the mcp-tooling skill first.
Install and self-check the bridge with bundled install.sh and a read-only doctor.sh that flags a missing aside UTCP manual registration as an error.
Call the live-verified aside.aside_repl(args) TypeScript callable (registry name aside.aside.repl) inside call_tool_chain.
Validate the setup with 15 manual-testing scenarios, including blind recall holdouts and troubleshooting coverage.

title: mcp-refero: read-only Refero design-reference transport
bullets: Search Refero's design-reference library (styles, screens, flows) read-only for UI research through a new mcp-tooling hub mode.
All eight Refero tools are callable via the confirmed doubled-prefix form (refero.refero_refero_<tool>), with a mandatory tool_info confirmation before use.
mcp-refero joins mcp-figma as the hub's second design transport, both paired with sk-design for reference-driven design work.
Plan gating applies: Refero's MCP surface needs a Pro plan (8,000 MCP calls/month) and Free tier has no MCP access, with live OAuth calls fenced to the operator.

title: mcp-mobbin: Mobbin design research in mcp-tooling hub
bullets: You can now research real mobile-app UI patterns — screens, flows, and sections — from Mobbin directly in-session through the new read-only mcp-mobbin transport mode on the mcp-tooling hub.
Three search tools (`search_screens`, `search_flows`, `search_sections`) are callable even before signing in, and access uses OAuth with no API key to store.
Flow search returns ordered results with per-screen previews and action counts, so you can trace real app navigation patterns instead of guessing.
As the hub's third design transport, mcp-mobbin pairs with sk-design so design judgment stays with the design skill while it supplies research.

title: mcp-tooling routing now correct and honest
bullets: Prompts to the mcp-tooling hub now land on the intended skill every time (13/13 scenarios vs 6/13 before), fixing missed or wrong routing for Figma, ClickUp, Obsidian, and the other modes.
When a prompt names no specific tool, the router now declines to guess and offers a disambiguation checklist alongside the suggested default instead of silently loading an arbitrary resource.

The Figma transport is now transparent about its writes: it declares no workspace mutation, scopes local exports behind a no-overwrite gate, and requires sk-design pairing before any design-affecting operation.
Skill-benchmark runs on hub-type skills now fail loudly (BLOCKED-BY-ROUTE-GOLD, exit 3) when any scenario routes to the wrong intent, so mis-routing can no longer hide behind a passing score.
The regenerated playbook index now covers all six modes and resolves every link, replacing a previous index where four links were broken.

title: MCP tooling docs aligned to canonical templates
bullets: The asIDE DevTools, Refero, and Mobbin packet docs now follow the repository's canonical overview and README structures, so you get predictable navigation across all three.
All three script READMEs were rebuilt to the full code-folder scaffold, lifting their documentation quality above the required floor.

Mobbin guidance now lists only the confirmed live tools (`search_screens`, `search_flows`, `search_sections`) and the client-settable `deep` mode, with authenticated OAuth behavior honestly labeled as unverified.
Every alignment lane passes with zero P0 and P1 findings, and package, link, and spec-folder validation all pass cleanly.

title: New mcp-obsidian mode: vault operations from the terminal
bullets: Operate Obsidian vaults from the terminal as a new mcp-tooling hub mode, routed across the headless notesmd-cli, the app-backed Obsidian CLI, and the Local REST API MCP server.
Create, read, move, delete and manage daily notes and frontmatter headlessly, verified against a live vault.
Get file-layer guidance for community plugins and themes including Beancount finance, Obsidian Tables, BRAT, Health.md, Dataview, and Excalidraw.
Inspect a current-state feature catalog and reproduce the operator test surface with a shipped manual-testing playbook.

title: Semantic code search across all AI CLIs
bullets: Find code by intent and concept (e.g. "authentication middleware") instead of needing exact identifiers for Grep/Glob.
The same semantic search works from all 6 AI CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode, agents) via one shared MCP server.
Search runs fully locally with no API key, so no code ever leaves your machine.
Semantic search can cut token usage 10-50x by replacing Grep-Read-Filter cascades for conceptual queries.
Readiness and bootstrap helpers (doctor/ensure-ready) verify the index and recover stale setups automatically.

title: Manual testing playbooks for MCP bridges
bullets: Verify the mcp-code-mode, mcp-chrome-devtools, and mcp-clickup bridges yourself with 75 per-feature test scenarios across 19 categories.
The mcp-coco-index playbook gained 3 gap-filling scenarios covering the concurrent refresh race, the root-path environment override, and helper-script readiness.
All four playbooks pass the validator, and real-environment smoke runs confirmed 3 of 4 bridges work (the ClickUp bridge was skipped on a machine without the CLI).

title: Figma MCP Agent replaces mcp-figma skill
bullets: Figma automation now runs through a dedicated Figma MCP Agent in AI_Systems (mirroring the ClickUp agent), shipped with a knowledge base and install guide for fast setup.
The agent is dual-published to AI_Systems/Public and listed in the Public README, so cross-team users can discover and adopt it.
The old in-workspace mcp-figma skill has been removed, so existing Figma workflows and references must point to the new agent.
